header: THE QUARTERLY IDA ORDERS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC ENTERPRISES, READ FROM ITS OWN WEBSITE (so the card no longer waits for me to type a new order in by hand). Every quarter DPE issues an Office Memorandum "Revision of Industrial Dearness Allowance (IDA) Rates for Executives and Non-Unionized Supervisors of CPSEs - effective from 01.10.2026", with the rate for each pay scale ("... shall be 489.5% for the 1997 pay scale, 249.2% for the 2007 pay scale, and 59.1% for the 2017 pay scale"). dpe.gov.in draws its pages in the browser from an open WordPress service (the same address the site itself calls: www.dpe.gov.in/cms/wp-json/wp/v2), whose list of central documents gives, for each order, the title (with the day it takes effect), the date it was put on the site and a link to the PDF. WHAT I TAKE: only the 2017 pay scale's rate, because that is the one the card is about (SAIL's executives); and only from the order's own words. WHAT I DO NOT DO: guess. The orders of April and July 2026 and of October 2025 are scanned pictures (no text in the PDF), and the order of October 2026 has a text layer; I read the rate where there is text, and where there is only a picture I give the order and its link and say the rate has to be read from it (the rates I read from the pictures by eye are in aicpi.ts, IDA_ANNOUNCED). A rate that is not a plausible one for the 2017 scales is thrown away, not shown. WHAT GOES OUT: fixed public addresses only; nothing typed by anybody.

symbols.name: loadDpeOrders
symbols.sig: export async function loadDpeOrders(deps: DpeDeps): Promise<DpeOrder[]>
doc: The newest quarterly orders with what could be read of each. An order that has been read is kept (its key holds its id and its "modified" time, so a re-posted order is read again). A failure of one order (its media record or its PDF) leaves that order with no rate and no link; a failure of the list is an empty answer. Nothing here throws.

symbols.name: forgetOrders
doc: For the tests: forget what is kept.

symbols.name: validOrders
symbols.sig: export function validOrders(x: unknown): x is DpeOrder[]

behaviours: DPE's list of 40 central documents gives the quarterly IDA orders of the executives, newest first: 1 Oct 2026, 1 Jul 2026, 1 Apr 2026, 1 Oct 2025 (the January 2026 order is not on DPE's site)
each order has the day DPE put it up and its PDF (the media record), the 2025 order that only says 'have been revised' and the earlier 'pay scales' documents are not taken
a record whose title has no day of effect, or a day that is not the first of a quarter, is not an order
what is not a list is an empty list; the same day put up twice keeps the later posting
the media record's PDF is taken only when it is a PDF on DPE's own site
the days in the orders are read: '27th October 2026', 'the 17th July 2026', '24.04.2026', '29th October, 2025'
the order of 27 Oct 2026: 59.1% for the 2017 scale (not the 489.5% of 1997 or the 249.2% of 2007), its number and its date
the words of April 2026 ('54.1% for the 2017 pay scale') and a table row ('2017 51.8%') are read as well
a picture (a PDF with no text) gives nothing; two different figures for the 2017 scale give nothing; a figure that is not plausible gives nothing
loading gives the four orders: October 2026 with its rate (59.1) and its PDF, the three scanned ones with their PDFs and no rate (a picture is not read)
an order that has been read is not read again: the second load asks only for the list
the media address is built from the PDF's id
a list that cannot be had gives an empty answer, not an error
a PDF that cannot be had leaves its order listed with no rate (it is asked again next time)
and the next load reads it
a media record that points outside DPE gives no link and no rate
